It's a long fucking post. You'll survive. Watch me crash and burn, you'll go from awe and amazement to shocked and appalled in just a few screenshots. If you're not keen to look at them all, start from Day 7. If you want to see just the crash and burn look at 10-13.

Disclaimer: I do NOT condone betting. It is risky. If you are under age you should not be betting period. I bet because I can afford the loss and my initial investment was minimal. At the end of all this I had a lot of fun full of tense moments while staying up late watching matches (most games are played between 11pm and 4am my time). I also only lost $45 (my initial investment in the Neon Rider and AK Elite build, which dropped a lot of value before I bet them).

Some images contain more than one 'day' of bets, mostly when there was little to be shown across a few days.

I would not recommend copying my bet strategy or ask me about future bets. My strategy was risky and eventually spread across 2 accounts (which is why some skins just disappear from this list, if you're keeping track). The only advice I can offer, if any, is to bet with an alternate account. They cannot access the in-game inventory (even with a steam share copy of CS:GO) and you can trade your good items to your main and get attached to them, therefore lowering the risk of you wanting to bet them. My Neon Rider had 1.5k kills on it when I first bet it :(

Day 1 - I started off pretty well. I didn't know much of what I was talking about yet having only watched the pro scene for a few weeks prior, but after a few years of betting on Dota 2 matches I had a rough idea of how accurate the %'s were, the risk/reward value of betting on Bo1's vs Bo3's etc.

I won my first few bets which netted me some low value bettables but ended the day with a loss. Not too bad a start.

 

Day 2 - As you can see I knew fairly well to bet on the side of Fnatic. Early days they netted me reliable bettables which I later used on risky bets. Lots of trash skins which will later be bet on 13% matches (which turns out pay out fairly well if it comes through!)

 

Day 3 - Another alright day, also the first bet I lost on Fnatic. Apologies for the mouseover, I cbf going back and fixing it at this stage, they are trash skins anyway. Nothing too impressive here, lots of small value skins to throw at low % matches later.

 

Day 4 - Win! Win! Win! Then my first losses on low % bets. As you can see, this early I didn't risk any "money" skins on risky bets. That changes pretty fast though as you'll see. Started winning skins worth around the $5-$7 mark here which brings my average win up as I can throw more value at safer bets.

 

Day 5 - Not a great day. Lost a fair bit, mostly trash again though so no trouble. Another good value bettable picked up (the Water Elemental, pulling $7.50 at the time).

 

Day 6 - Today was a good day! This is where some of my risky bets paid off. I picked up my first skins worth over $12, the AK Vulcans, AWP Asiimov, ST Fire Elemental and some other good bettables. I missed a match in here, NiP vs Dignitas which was a medium value bet ($9 or so) on a low win %. At this stage I could afford to lose some of my midrange bettables since I could win them back easy with safe bets.

 

Day 7 - Win, win and more wins. Another decent day at the races. Played mostly safe bets this day, as is evident by my minimal winnings. Lost a low value bet and also one of the AK's I picked up the day before. At this stage I told myself "I'll keep one of each skin and bet doubles!" which is why I wasn't too bummed about losing the AK Vulcan. I wish I'd saved the Cartel though. This is the day I learned to bet AGAINST Nihilum, which will later pay off.

 

Day 8 - Today I start playing a bit risky. The closed bets were those with a close % win or loss (both teams within 10-15% of 50) and Bo2's. I find that Bo2's are fairly reliable to bet on the lower of the two teams since you get your skins back if they manage at least one map. Hopefully they'll win at least their map pick. As you can see, playing the Bo2's paid off in the sense that I didn't lose anything. Played a safe bet and picked up another AWP Asiimov, which would bring my safe bet win average up.

By this stage I was placing bets based on the return I would get. I was aiming at a $50 win since that would net me either: an AWP Asiimov or a $25-$35 skin + more bettables.

 

Day 9 - As you can see I'm playing the Bo2 game again today. It pays off by returning my items without a loss. A stale but otherwise positive result. I won all my other bets, mostly safies, bar one low % win chance which you can see I threw low value items at.

 

Day 10 - The day started out a bit rough, 3 losses straight. Luckily they were cheap bets! Ended on a high, picking up another 2 AWP Asiimov's and some other good value bettables which will bring my risky bet win value up when I get around to it.

 

Day 11 - Knives! Knives! Knives! So many knives! Holy shit this was a fantastic day. One knife appears out of nowhere, the flip knife. I think I won it on my 2nd account which I started using around now to double up my low cost bets on low % wins. Low risk with double the return. If you have a bunch (I'm talking 30-40 of them) of trash skins ($0.05-$1 value) then spreading them across multiple accounts and doubling/tripling up on low % bets (that you think you have a chance of winning) can pay off.

I cop a couple of big losses today as well. The loss between HR and G2 was brutal, being my first bet placed over $150 value. It hurt to lose, but the desire to win grew stronger. Two of my risky bets paid off, AceG v Nihilum (remember how I mentioned I learned to bet AGAINST those guys, yeah. Fuck Nihilum. Sorry boys, ya suck) and G2 v Na'Vi.

Starseries was a good tournament to bet on since Fnatic wasn't around and even the higher tier teams were getting smashed in Bo1's. Unfortunately G2, Gside etc didn't pull through when it came to Bo3's but they did fantastically and that was the basis of some of my riskier bets, those teams were on FIRE!

All in all I probably came out $100-$200 on top. I lost the knives the same day I got them, on "safe" bets no less. I think I ended with two knives, the Gut Knife and the Huntsman.

 

Day 12 - I are winning knife, yes? Yeah I did. I picked up 2 knives on my other account, which by now was armed with some Asiimov's from the winnings the day before. So many knives today! Possibly my best day on record, seriously. I had 3 plain Flip Knives at one point today, so I considered them to be bettables to throw at low % bets. You don't see me lose them all in these pics, nor do you see me lose all the AWP's, but I guarantee I lost them on my other account. I started losing safe bets, repeatedly.

A number of my bets paid off today on this account. I was in pretty deep with 2x accounts by now so my losses look a lot lower than they actually were. That HR v Na'Vi game? I probably lost another $100 on it by doubling up.

My overall inventory value peaked this day or the day before. IIRC I had about 6 Asiimov's, 8 knives, a ST AK worth $55 (~~can't remember which skin~~ Jaguar!) and a bunch of nice skins around $20-$35 value to use. I had previously disliked the AWP Asiimov but fell in love with the M4A4 and P90 Asiimov skins. The P90 in particular I think is fantastic. I miss it.

 

Day 13 - More commonly known as "Aaaaand it's gone" day! I'd lost a few AWP's and a knife or 2 on my other account. This is where true addiction prevails. If you check my post history you'll see I'm an addict, always gotta have something to go on. Anyway, I digress.

This day consisted of a mix of safe bets and some risky bets. None of them paid off. I lost 6 knives in 3 days, sure they weren't the best of knives but they were pretty good. Also worth noting here is I gave 2 knives to mates who don't really invest in cosmetics. One Gut Knife Forest DDPAT and one of the Flip Knives (I think it was the painted one, not sure which pattern it was).

Anyway, you can see the disaster here. At the end of this I have no skins over $1 value. You'll notice the lack of AWP Asiimov's being lost, despite many being won. Yeah, remember that 2nd account? I doubled down on a lot of losses this day I think. Ultimately, this was shit. There goes what, $400 in a few days. I'll dig up the other account and post pics if people are interested, matching the bets between the accounts.

At the end of all this I learned a valuable lesson. Betting is fun! Seriously though, it can be addictive and crippling. Imagine if I had invested $400 in skins then lost it. Might as well have pissed it up against a wall. $400 might not be a lot to many people, but to others it's a fortune. All depends on where you are in life.

I have sold my Dota 2 inventory and have started betting again, starting today. I had a bunch of $1-$2 AK skins. So far I have tripled my investment, having lost only 2 bets. I lost one bet that was my first "big" bet at $22, which was a bit of a kick in the guts. If you are interested in updates on my current bets I can do an update every 2 days.

I currently have a $60 bet being played, which will win me $58. It's a bit of a risky bet, but I chose this team because I saw them convincingly win 2-0 earlier and they are in another Bo3 (LoG.kz)

I think that people might be led a bit by the word "Sequence." People will therefore almost always type their numbers in a sequential order from lowest to highest, which means they may test many theories, all of which will invariably be correct simply because they sort the numbers before entering them.
Even if you are mislead by the word "Sequence", you could test [1, 1, 1] or something similar.

We used to get these questions at school and you were always looking for N where N is the next number in the sequence. I felt pre-programmed to look for the pattern as most people are and so I figured it's the internet it'll be a trick and went another route which paid off. My wife didn't and checked once before going straight to knowing the answer, incorrectly.

I realize the desire to be right is inherent in human nature, but I'm wondering if there isn't a social/cultural aspect as well. Would someone who is routinely told they're "bad" or "wrong" be more likely to ask incorrect answers than someone who is usually told they're "good"? Heck, would someone with generally low self esteem be more likely to ask "no" answers, because they don't trust their own judgement, or would they still go for "yes", because of the normal desire to be correct?

The rule was simply: Each number must be larger than the one before it.

Wrong. Each number must be larger than the one before it, and the largest number must be less than 10000000000000000.

You can also provide negative numbers; the smallest allowable number is somewhere between -10000000000000000 and -210000000000000000.

Because it's mostly quiet on the Bromeliad front on the web. I've been geeked out on this family of plants for a few years now and have spent many hours sifting through sites to get information on obscure specimens I've picked up along the way. I have almost no expectation for this subverse to go anywhere beyond mildly active for a few reasons: 1) It's a narrow niche in and of itself, 2) /r/Bromeliads never got any real traction, 3) the most active online community I found around bromeliads is on the gardenweb forums and even there the posts trickle in with days in between, 4) voat is still a pup, not many users here yet. Please don't take this as a lack of enthusiasm for this sub, just keeping expectations in check. I'll keep submitting interesting articles and topics to keep this going, and maybe, just maybe, a few of you will also get hooked on these fascinating organisms and contribute as well.

One common source I see that brings people to these specific botanical communities is identifying specimens. This comes up a lot within this family because of Tillandsias, better known as air plants. Greenhouses are littered with all sorts of tillandsias and people often want to know what species they acquired and how to care for it. So by all means dump any ID requests here, I'll do my best to assist.

Enjoy your stay, and good growing to you all ;)
